extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators and State drinking water program staff (EPA Lead and Copper Rule compliance)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements governing sampling, monitoring frequency, analytical methods, waivers, reporting, and State interactions for lead and copper in drinking water and associated water quality parameters under the EPA Lead and Copper Rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sample timing and location rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement samples taken after invalidation must be taken no later than the end of the tap sampling period or by the time the system notifies the State of an invalidated sample, whichever occurs later. Replacement samples taken after the end of the applicable tap sampling period can only be used to meet the monitoring requirements of the applicable tap monitoring period and not a subsequent period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement samples must be taken at the same locations as the invalidated samples, except when the sample was invalidated due to an error in meeting the site selection criteria or inability to gain access; in those cases replacement samples must be taken at locations that meet the site selection criteria other than locations already used during the tap monitoring period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver eligibility overview for systems ≤3,300 persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Any water system serving 3,300 or fewer persons may apply in writing to the State to reduce monitoring frequency for lead and/or copper to once every nine years if it meets the materials criteria and monitoring criteria specified in paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems can apply for a lead-only waiver, copper-only waiver, or a full waiver (both contaminants) depending on which criteria they meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials criteria for lead waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for a lead waiver, the water system must certify and provide supporting documentation to the State that the system, including the distribution system and all premise plumbing, is free of all lead-containing materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (A) contains no plastic pipes with lead plasticizers or plastic service lines with lead plasticizers; and (B) is free of lead service lines, galvanized requiring replacement service lines, lead connectors, lead pipes, lead soldered pipe joints, and leaded brass or bronze alloy fittings and fixtures, unless such fittings/fixtures meet specifications established pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 300g-6(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials criteria for copper waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for a copper waiver, the water system must certify and provide supporting documentation to the State that the system contains no copper service lines or premise plumbing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring criteria for waivers (90th percentile thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: System must have completed at least one six-month round of standard tap water monitoring at State-approved sites and demonstrate that the 90th percentile levels for monitoring conducted since the system became free of lead/copper meet specified thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead waiver: 90th percentile lead ≤ 0.005 mg/L. Copper waiver: 90th percentile copper ≤ 0.65 mg/L.

rubrics_metrics.name: State approval of waiver application and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The State must notify the system in writing of its waiver determination, set forth the basis of its decision and any conditions of an approved waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a condition of a waiver, the State may require activities (e.g., limited monitoring, periodic outreach to customers) to avoid concentrations of concern. The water system must continue monitoring as required under paragraphs (c) and (d) until it receives written notification that a waiver has been approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency and certification requirements for systems with waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: A system with a full waiver must conduct tap monitoring for lead and copper at least once every nine years and provide the State with the materials certification when submitting tap sampling results; samples collected every nine years must be collected no later than every ninth calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system with a single-contaminant waiver (lead or copper) must conduct tap monitoring for only the waived contaminant at least once every nine years and provide certification for only the waived contaminant. Systems must notify the State in writing about any addition of a new source water or long-term change in treatment; the State may modify waiver conditions. If a system becomes aware it is no longer free of the relevant materials, it must notify the State in writing within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver discontinuation/ineligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A system with a waiver is not allowed to continue monitoring under its waiver if certain conditions occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (i) Full or lead waiver: no longer satisfies lead materials criteria or 90th percentile lead > 0.005 mg/L; (ii) Full or copper waiver: no longer satisfies copper materials criteria or 90th percentile copper > 0.65 mg/L; (iii) State notifies the system in writing that the waiver has been revoked with basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements following waiver revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A system whose waiver is revoked may re-apply when it meets the appropriate materials and monitoring criteria and is subject to corrosion control treatment and monitoring requirements following revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the system exceeds lead/copper action levels it must implement or re-optimize OCCT per §141.81 deadlines; if at or below both action levels, it must monitor at the tap no less frequently than once every three years using the reduced number of sampling sites in paragraph (d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-existing waivers continuation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Waivers approved by the State prior to the compliance date remain in effect if the system has demonstrated it meets materials and monitoring criteria and does not meet waiver ineligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of tap monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems must make tap monitoring results, including data used in the 90th percentile calculation, publicly accessible within 60 days of the end of the tap sampling period unless done by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems are not required to make addresses of tap sampling sites public. Large systems must make results and associated data publicly accessible in digital format; small and medium systems may use print or digital. Systems must certify compliance in writing to the State and retain monitoring data per recordkeeping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of water quality parameter monitoring (§141.87 applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: All large water systems and all medium water systems with corrosion control treatment (unless deemed optimized), and all small and medium systems that exceed the lead or copper action level must sample and monitor water quality parameters in addition to lead and copper as required by this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any system may be required to monitor water quality parameters as determined by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representativeness and site selection for distribution system sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution system samples collected at water taps must be representative of water quality throughout the distribution system, considering number of persons served, different sources, different treatment methods, and seasonal variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sites selected can be same or different from lead/copper tap sites and may consider total coliform sampling sites. Sites must be included in the site sample plan and updated prior to changes to sampling locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters required for distribution system analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples collected in the distribution system must be analyzed for pH, alkalinity, orthophosphate (as PO4) when an orthophosphate inhibitor is used, silica when a silicate inhibitor is used, and any parameters specified by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry point sampling representativeness and parameter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry point samples must be from locations representative of each source water after treatment; if multiple sources are combined before distribution, sample at an entry point representative of all sources during normal operating conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At each entry point measure pH; if alkalinity is adjusted measure dosage rate and alkalinity concentration; if corrosion inhibitor used measure dosage rate and concentration of orthophosphate or silica; and any State-specified parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of distribution system sampling sites and sample counts (Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect two distribution system samples for applicable parameters during each monitoring period from each of the minimum number of sites listed in Table 1, with additional sites from Distribution System and Site Assessment added up to a maximum of twice the minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry point sampling frequency rules depending on OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems without installed or re-optimized OCCT and without State-designated optimal parameters required to collect entry point samples must collect a minimum of two entry point samples for each applicable parameter at each entry point at least once during each monitoring period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems with installed or re-optimized OCCT and/or State-designated optimal parameters required to collect entry point samples must collect one entry point sample for each applicable parameter at each entry point at least once every two weeks during each monitoring period the system is required to conduct sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial sampling timing and parameters for water quality parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Large systems without corrosion control must begin monitoring during the first two six-month monitoring periods beginning no later than January 1 after becoming large or exceeding the PQL for lead. Medium and small systems that exceed action levels must begin monitoring for two consecutive six-month monitoring periods beginning the month after the end of the tap monitoring period in which the action level exceedance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At distribution sites collect two samples for pH and alkalinity; at each entry point collect all applicable parameters listed for entry points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring after installation or re-optimization of OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that modifies or installs OCCT and is required to conduct follow-up monitoring must monitor applicable distribution system and entry point water quality parameters every six months until the State designates new parameter values for OCCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples must be collected at a regular frequency throughout the six-month monitoring period to reflect seasonal variability. Groundwater systems may limit entry point sampling to representative entry points but must provide documentation to the State demonstrating representativeness. States may require small systems to monitor or develop their own monitoring structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring with State-designated optimal water quality parameter values
rubrics_metrics.description: Medium water systems with corrosion control and all large water systems must sample for State-designated parameters every six months and determine compliance as specified under §141.82(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small systems with corrosion control that exceed action levels must begin monitoring during the standard six-month tap monitoring period immediately following the exceedance and continue until they no longer exceed action levels and meet State-designated optimal parameters in two consecutive six-month tap monitoring periods. States may require continued monitoring at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced monitoring eligibility and reduced minimum sites (Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A medium or large system that maintains the range of values for water quality parameters reflecting OCCT specified by the State and does not exceed action levels in either of two consecutive six-month monitoring periods may collect two distribution system samples from each of the reduced minimum number of sites listed in Table 2 during each six-month monitoring period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 reduced minimums: >100,000: 10; 10,001–100,000: 7; 3,301–10,000: 3; 501–3,300: 2; 101–500: 1; ≤100: 1. Systems with added sites from assessments must continue sampling up to twice the minimum number in Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to reduce monitoring frequency to annual
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that maintains the range of values for State-designated OCCT parameters and does not exceed action levels for three consecutive years may reduce distribution system sampling frequency from every six months to annually starting the calendar year after the third year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, a system may reduce to annual sampling if during two consecutive monitoring periods its tap water 90th percentile lead ≤ PQL 0.005 mg/L and 90th percentile copper ≤ 0.65 mg/L and it has maintained required parameter ranges. Annual samples must be collected at a regular frequency throughout the year to reflect seasonal variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resuming standard monitoring upon noncompliance during reduced monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A system monitoring at a reduced frequency that fails to operate within the range of optimal water quality parameters for more than nine cumulative days in any six-month period must resume distribution system sampling per standard number/frequency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a system may resume annual monitoring at the reduced number of sites after completing two subsequent consecutive six-month rounds of monitoring that meet the reduced criteria or after demonstrating compliance with the conditions allowing annual monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceedance rules for reduced frequency systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system monitoring at a reduced frequency that exceeds the lead or copper action level must resume standard water quality parameter monitoring beginning with the six-month period immediately following the tap monitoring period in which the action level exceedance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the system no longer exceeds action levels and meets State-designated optimal parameters in two consecutive six-month periods, it may reduce monitoring again per applicable paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of additional monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of any monitoring conducted in addition to the minimum requirements must be considered by the water system and the State in determining concentrations of water quality parameters under this section or §141.82.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water sampling locations and compositing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a system fails to meet tap action levels it shall collect source water samples at entry points representative of each source after treatment. Groundwater and surface systems must take a minimum of one sample at each entry point, generally at the same sampling point unless another is more representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may allow compositing (max five samples) by certified lab personnel. If a composite sample's lead ≥ 0.001 mg/L or copper ≥ 0.160 mg/L then either follow-up sampling at each point within 14 days or use duplicates/originals if available instead of resampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation sampling and reporting of below-detection values
rubrics_metrics.description: If sampling indicates an exceedance of maximum permissible source water levels the State may require one additional sample within two weeks at the same sampling point; results of initial and confirmation are averaged for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any sample value below the detection limit is considered zero. Any value above the detection limit but below the PQL may be considered as the measured value or one-half the PQL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water monitoring timing after tap exceedance and waiver conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that exceeds lead/copper action levels at the tap must collect one source water sample from each entry point no later than six months after the end of the tap sampling period in which the exceedance occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may waive source water monitoring if: (i) system already conducted source monitoring following a previous exceedance; (ii) State determined source water treatment is not required; and (iii) system has not added any new water sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source water monitoring after installation of source water treatment or addition of new source
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that install source water treatment must collect one source water sample from each entry point during two consecutive six-month monitoring periods by the specified deadline. Systems that add a new source must collect one source water sample from each entry point until they demonstrate finished drinking water entering distribution remains below State-specified maximum permissible concentrations or the State determines treatment is not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency when State specifies maximum permissible source water levels
rubrics_metrics.description: If the State specifies maximum permissible source water levels, groundwater-only systems shall collect samples once during the three-year compliance period and every third calendar year thereafter; surface-water systems shall collect samples once during each calendar year, beginning in the year the State determination is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system is not required to conduct source water sampling if it meets the action level for the contaminant in tap samples during the entire applicable source water sampling period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced source water monitoring eligibility and criteria (nine-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: A groundwater-only system may reduce source water monitoring to once every nine-year compliance cycle if samples are collected no later than every ninth calendar year and the system demonstrates finished drinking water entering distribution has been maintained below State-specified maximum permissible concentrations during at least three consecutive monitoring periods. Surface-water or combined systems may similarly reduce provided finished water has been maintained below levels for at least three consecutive years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system using a new source is not eligible for reduced monitoring until concentrations in samples from the new source during three consecutive monitoring periods are below State-specified maximum permissible concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods for lead, copper, pH, alkalinity, orthophosphate, silica
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses shall be conducted in accordance with methods in §141.23(k)(1). Alkalinity, orthophosphate, pH, and silica may be performed by any person acceptable to the State. Analyses for lead and copper must only be conducted by laboratories certified by EPA or the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain certification labs must analyze Performance Evaluation samples (including lead and copper) at least once a year by each desired method and achieve acceptance limits: Lead: ±30% of actual amount when actual ≥ 0.005 mg/L (PQL lead = 0.005 mg/L). Copper: ±10% when actual ≥ 0.050 mg/L (PQL copper = 0.050 mg/L). Labs must achieve a method detection limit for lead of 0.001 mg/L per appendix B of part 136 and be currently certified by EPA or the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously collected monitoring data
rubrics_metrics.description: States have authority to allow use of previously collected monitoring data for monitoring purposes if the data were collected and analyzed in accordance with requirements of this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rules for values between PQL and MDL and below MDL
rubrics_metrics.description: All lead and copper levels measured between the PQL and MDL must either be reported as measured or reported as one-half the PQL. All levels below the respective MDLs must be reported as zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: lead between PQL and MDL reported as measured or one-half PQL (PQL = 0.005 mg/L, MDL = 0.001 mg/L); copper between PQL and MDL reported as measured or one-half PQL (0.025 mg/L); copper/below-MDL report zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site sample plan and sample instruction reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: By the start of a system's first lead and copper tap monitoring period, water systems must submit to the State: a site sample plan including lists of tap sample site locations for lead/copper and site lists for water quality parameter monitoring; and a copy of the sample collection instructions provided to individuals who sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to the site sample plan require submission of an updated plan before the next tap sampling period. The State may require modifications. Systems with lead/galvanized/unknown status service lines must evaluate tap sampling locations prior to each tap period and submit updates if evaluations result in changes. Systems that cannot identify enough sampling sites must submit documentation (including customer refusals) that support the conclusion before the next tap period. If sample collection instructions are modified, updated versions must be submitted to the State prior to the next tap sampling period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reporting monitoring results
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system must report specified information for all lead and copper tap samples and for all water quality parameter distribution system and entry point samples within the first 10 days following the end of each applicable sampling period, unless the State has specified an earlier reporting requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reporting requirement is notwithstanding §141.31(a).
